sentences: Dispatched like `s_cselect_b64`: when destination is `exec`/`vcc` or any source is a lane mask (`holds_lane_mask` or `exec`/`vcc`), uses the per-lane mask path (`mask_src`/`mask_dst` including `null` dst) and votes SCC across the wave (`scc_from_mask`).

Otherwise operates on both 32-bit dwords of non-mask 64-bit scalar data (SGPR pairs, sign-extended inline/literal immediates, `null` = 0), reads all source dwords before storing (preserving destination aliasing), accepts `null` destination, and sets `SCC = ((D.lo \ | D.hi) != 0)`.
Until 2026-11-22 these ops always took the lane-mask path, duplicating D.lo into D.hi and voting SCC on D.lo alone.
`s_nand/nor/xnor_b64` compute `~(S0 op S1)` on both paths (a lane's mask value is 0 or ~0, so the NOT is per lane); until 2026-11-22 they were rejected as unsupported.
